Where the evidence reaches.

The site supports documented hockey workflows used in Canadian rinks. It is not a complete Canadian installed-equipment roster. A brand report or product available in Canada does not prove an exact console model is installed at a rink.

Ontario

Multiple playable profiles; mostly association guides, including historical Cambridge evidence.

British Columbia

VisionTime at Panorama and Nevco MPC-4 evidence; Scoretec at Coquitlam.

Alberta

Scoretec and Nevco evidence in Calgary; code-871 guide names four Edmonton arenas.

Quebec

Ringette Laval reports Nevco at Yvon-Chartrand and OES at Place Bell. These are ringette sources; exact hardware and hockey configuration mapping remain unresolved.

Playable profiles and their limits.

Checked 25 October 2026. Local guides may describe older equipment. Read the installed model label and hockey overlay before selecting a simulator.

Daktronics All Sport 5000Mitchell, Ontario; Carleton University, Ottawa

Read rink evidence ↗

Hockey overlay LL-2436; installed firmware can differ. Minor/major additive penalty presets and penalty indicators are modelled. Team timeout counts, player-penalty recall editing, setup menus and auxiliary shot timers remain omitted.

Operating document ↗

Nevco MPC-4 · K2-28Kitsilano, British Columbia

Read rink evidence ↗

Hockey overlay K2-28, configuration 008-3261. No shot clocks. Alternate switch works only with no handheld attached. Ten penalties per side are a trainer limit; hardware has larger per-player memory. Clock modes here expose local time only; automatic startup programs and auxiliary clocks are omitted. Exact-score entry follows the local single-digit guide, with TIME returning to the clock.

Operating document ↗

Nevco MPCW-7Russell, Ontario; Don Hartman North East Sportsplex, Calgary, Alberta

Read rink evidence ↗

Additional regional evidence ↗

2016 hockey overlay, wired panel time control with no handheld attached. Default minor 2:00, major 5:00; penalty on/off enabled. Main MMSSs commits after five digits; period is separate. Timeout timer 1 is fixed to 30 seconds, displayed on the practice scoreboard; warning options and other timeout timers are omitted. Radio pairing, profiles, installation options, team-name programming and shot clocks are outside this profile. Goal light duration is a practice default.

Operating document ↗

Fair-Play MP-50 / MP-70Ray Twinney / Hollingsworth, Newmarket (MP-70 named in undated guide); Ray Friel, Ottawa (family only)

Read rink evidence ↗

MP-50/70 common hockey workflow; fixed 2/5/10-minute presets, five penalties per side, no 10-minute indicator spots, goal indicators enabled. The manufacturer photo shows the housing with a basketball overlay. Hockey key groups are a functional training arrangement; exact hockey overlay positions remain unverified. OTHER multi-segment penalties, program menus, timeout configuration, interval configuration, shifted penalty tracking and automatic penalty-time correction are omitted. Correcting the main clock preserves penalty times in this trainer.

Operating document ↗

Scoretec Ultimatic U1000Coquitlam, British Columbia; Calgary, Alberta

Read rink evidence ↗

U1000 control family with shots and player-number display, as described in the manufacturer manual. Five penalty slots per team, two active. Staging uses minutes or M:SS with optional /player. Long holds on CLEAR and STOP/GO PENALTIES take five seconds. Interval mode 1 and count-up limit mode 2 are implemented; full interval programming, time-of-day setup and team timeouts are omitted. Naden appears in the hosted manual title; that does not establish that every Naden console is a U1000.

Operating document ↗

Harris Time SportstimerCambridge, Ontario: Dickson, Duncan McIntosh, Hespeler and Preston (2016 guide)

Read rink evidence ↗

Photographed Cambridge Sportstimer variant; unlocked at the start of practice. TIME and INT accept up to 20:00; periods 0–4; penalties up to five slots per side. Practice scoreboard displays two active slots and queues the rest. Slot labels stand in for player numbers because this panel enters a slot, not a jersey. Manual horn uses HORN 0 #; 2/3-minute horn must be configured each period. Exact Type 1 versus Type 2 mapping is unverified. HI indicator programming, passkey and physical unlock behavior are omitted.

Operating document ↗

Rotomatic A3004-PTKarl Homuth Arena, Cambridge, Ontario (2016 guide)

Read rink evidence ↗

Legacy A3004-PT label visible in the local guide photograph. Separate tens/units score buttons and two physical penalty timers per team, without jersey entry or an automatic queue. MAIN TIME switch plus START arms the clock. AUTO HORN is the interval toggle, separate from the automatic five-second end horn. Main RESET also sounds the horn. Mechanical key auto-repeat, electromechanical latency and contact behavior are not emulated. No manufacturer manual located; operation is sourced to the local rink guide and photographed panel instructions.

Operating document ↗
